items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: like Sarah Vaughan, like Billie Holiday, Nat King Cole. They have that certain something in their voices

ctx.x: You know I wanted to make just one comment about some of the things that you’ve said and what you’ve been telling us about the blues lyrics is that I sense in your music this marvelous sense of humor. Do you think we could have more of that in music today? I think music needs some of that to come back.

I think it would be nice to have some kind of sense of humor in your music as well as seriousness when it comes to like playing say like “My Funny Valentine” or something like that. You can really make a person feel like this is my valentine. Or if you play like “Lover Man” you want to get that same kind of feeling that Billie Holiday had because it © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

was something very unique and very few people are able to capture that type of feelings anymore. She just had that certain voice. And if you notice, there are certain people that come along, maybe every two decades, and they will have like, well, like Sarah Vaughan, like Billie Holiday, Nat King Cole. They have that certain something in their voices, you know, Ella Fitzgerald, there’s just something — that’s another person that’s alive now, that’s still alive, Gloria Lynne, she’s another that has that certain —…
